day_shape: 94 items: OFAC publishes final rule amending Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations plus new GLs, State Department designates one Iranian and two Russian entities for military procurement, tanker struck in Strait of Hormuz, Araghchi receives US 7-day trust-building feedback via Qatar, and Netanyahu tells UAE that Iran is renewing its nuclear programme.

threads.label: US sanctions and OFAC rulemaking on Iran
threads.summary: OFAC published a final rule amending the Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations to implement provisions of the January 2020 Executive Order, alongside Iran-related General Licenses X and X1. The State Department separately designated one Iran-based and two Russia-based entities for facilitating Iranian military procurement, with additional sanctions targeting 10 individuals and entities in China, Hong Kong and Pakistan.

threads.label: US-Iran diplomatic track via Qatar
threads.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi received US feedback on a seven-day trust-building plan through Qatari mediators and will discuss it in Tehran. Trump denied a report he was prepared to offer sanctions relief and frozen fund release, while Axios reported talks had reached a diplomatic stalemate that could resume fighting after US midterm elections.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz and maritime incidents
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported a tanker struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, and Turkish bailiffs seized a Caspian Airlines Boeing 737 at Istanbul airport over debt recovery. IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohbi told Iranian television that clashes were ongoing in the Strait of Hormuz and that Americans had not responded for some time.

threads.label: Sacred Defence Week messaging cycle
threads.summary: Khamenei's office and Defa Press ran a heavy cycle of Sacred Defence Week content, including the Supreme Leader's message on armed readiness and the anniversary of Hassan Nasrallah's killing. Passive Defence chief Brigadier General Gholamreza Jalali gave a four-part interview describing wartime preparations across 46 operational systems and upcoming defence exercises.

threads.label: Iranian executions and internal security
threads.summary: Iran executed two men, Majid Nik Bakhsh and Ali Hamati, over the December 1404 Tabarsi incident in Mashhad that killed four security personnel, according to Defa Press and IRIB. Iran International reported a German-based aid worker received a 10-year prison sentence, and hardliners intensified attacks on Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf and Chief Justice Mohseni-Ejei following lawmaker Rasaei's imprisonment.

threads.label: Israel, Gaza and regional security
threads.summary: Netanyahu told UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed that Israeli intelligence shows Iran is renewing its nuclear programme, while Palestinian media reported at least four killed in an IDF strike on a Gaza City minibus. Syrian Internal Security Forces claimed to have arrested a three-person Hezbollah cell, and Hamas, PIJ and Mohammed Dahlan announced an electoral coalition for November's Palestinian Legislative Council vote.

events.title_en: Discovery of over 600 kilogrammes of narcotics in 'City Calm' operation in West Azerbaijan
events.summary_en: Discovery of over 600 kilogrammes of narcotics in 'City Calm' operation in West Azerbaijan. Following implementation of the special 'City Calm' plan by West Azerbaijan Province's anti-narcotics police over the past four days, in a wide-ranging operation, 616 kilogrammes of various narcotics and over 7,000 unauthorised pills were discovered and seized. Commander Jamal Salmani of the provincial police announced the dismantling of 4 smuggling gangs, the arrest of 7 smugglers, the seizure of 15 vehicles, and the identification of 156 small-scale dealers and 286 open drug users (with focus on school areas and educational centres). He stressed the continuation of security operations to maintain city calm and urged citizens to cooperate in reporting suspicious cases.
